 Follow Hilary Swank Hits Back at ‘Geriatric’ Pregnancy Criticism at 52
 Deepshikha Sarkar Tue, November 17, 2026 at 5:58 PM UTC 2 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. Photo Credit: Raymond Hall/Getty Images Hilary Swank has responded to criticism over having a baby at 52, arguing that having children later in life is becoming increasingly common. The Oscar -winning actress, who is expecting her third child with husband Philip Schneider , also urged people to "get with the times" during an appearance on This Morning.
 Hilary Swank defends her decision to welcome third child
 During Tuesday's interview, host Cat Deeley recalled being labelled a "geriatric mum" after welcoming her youngest son at 42. In response, Swank defended later pregnancies, saying, "It's time to get with the times! We're so advanced in our world, people are living so much longer and so many women are wanting to wait until later, it's becoming quite a normal thing to have children later."
 The actress welcomed twins Aya and Ohm in April 2023 at 48. She said carrying one baby has been easier than carrying twins. During her previous pregnancy, she worked 18-hour days and used two body doubles because they could not work overtime. "But the pregnant, geriatric lady could!" she joked.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Swank also said she feels fortunate to have focused on her acting career before motherhood. "My career really was a baby of mine I wanted to give to, I didn't want distractions. I wanted to give to that. And now, I have both, and I feel so blessed," she said. She also shared that her twins are excited about the new arrival and keep asking when the baby will come. She tells them the baby will arrive around Christmas.
 The actress kept her pregnancy private until she was seven months along. She continued working until she was around 17 weeks pregnant without anyone on set knowing. Speaking on the Question Everything podcast, she explained, "I'm a pretty private person, and there was no reason to really, I don't know, say anything," as reported by Daily Mail .
 Swank previously told The Drew Barrymore Show that pregnancy does not always follow personal timelines. She explained, "This was the right time for me. Not everything happens in our own time. We have ideas for timelines for ourselves, and getting pregnant isn't always in our own timeline, right?"
 She also told PEOPLE that although she had always wanted children, circumstances delayed her journey to motherhood. Becoming a parent later in life has allowed her to be more present and approach parenting differently than she might have in her 20s or 30s.
